source.title: Adaptive gain and the role of the locus coeruleus-norepinephrine system in optimal performance

confidence_rationale: Canonical account of a low-dimensional MODE variable (LC-NE tonic vs phasic gain) that does bidirectional explore/exploit arbitration -- including switching exploration OFF to consolidate exploitation, the half a novelty bonus cannot provide. Biological/modelling, transfer by analogy.
failure_signatures: A per-step novelty bonus can only push exploration UP; it cannot switch exploration off and consolidate into competent exploitation -- the phasic-mode half of adaptive gain.

mapping.source_claim_statement: LC neurons occupy two dissociable modes -- phasic (fires to task-relevant outcomes, locking in exploitation) and tonic (elevated baseline, disengages the current task and drives search) -- with ACC/OFC monitoring utility to set which mode is active: a top-down gain/mode signal governing the explore<->exploit regime.
mapping.ree_translation: Motivates a scalar mode/gain variable that modulates policy stochasticity/commitment conditioned on critic-derived utility -- adding bidirectional arbitration (raise exploration when utility wanes, sharpen into exploitation when found), orthogonal to and composable with an RND bonus.
mapping.mapping_caveat: Monkey neurophysiology + modelling of arousal/gain, not a demonstration of closing a competence gap in an RL forager; the transfer is by analogy.
mapping.source_context: Primate locus-coeruleus neurophysiology + adaptive-gain computational theory.

confidence_components.notes: Strong mechanistic account but transfer to an RL competence gap is by analogy; the distinctive 'consolidate into exploitation' capability is the key contribution.
